origin.description: Estimates a probability density, a regression function, or their derivatives using local polynomials. A fast binned implementation over an equally spaced grid is used.
origin.usage:
locpoly(x, y, drv = 0L, degree, kernel = "normal",
        bandwidth, gridsize = 401L, bwdisc = 25,
        range.x, binned = FALSE, truncate = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector of x data. Missing values are not accepted.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Vector of y data, the same length as x. If omitted, a density estimate is computed. Missing values are not accepted.

arguments.name: drv
arguments.text: Order of derivative to be estimated.

arguments.name: degree
arguments.text: Degree of the local polynomial. Must be at least drv. The default is drv + 1.

arguments.name: kernel
arguments.text: "normal", the Gaussian density. Currently ignored.

arguments.name: bandwidth
arguments.text: Kernel bandwidth. A single number, or a vector of length gridsize for a bandwidth that varies with location.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of equally spaced grid points.

arguments.name: bwdisc
arguments.text: Number of logarithmically spaced bandwidths on which bandwidth is discretised.

arguments.name: range.x
arguments.text: Minimum and maximum values of x at which to compute the estimate.

arguments.name: binned
arguments.text: If TRUE, x and y are taken to be grid counts rather than raw data.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If TRUE, data outside range.x are ignored.

origin.details: Local polynomial fitting with a kernel weight estimates a density, a regression function, or their derivatives. Density estimation bins the data and fits the bin counts. Either way, an equally spaced grid makes the computation fast. The bandwidth may be a scalar or a vector of length gridsize.
origin.value: If y is given, a local polynomial regression estimate of E[Y|X] or its derivative. If y is omitted, a local polynomial estimate of the density of x or its derivative. The result is a list with x, the grid, and y, the smoothed estimates.
origin.example:
if(length(data(geyser, package="MASS"))) {
# local linear density estimate
x <- geyser$duration
est <- locpoly(x, bandwidth = 0.25)
plot(est, type = "l")

# local linear regression estimate
y <- geyser$waiting
plot(x, y)
fit <- locpoly(x, y, bandwidth = 0.25)
lines(fit)
}

translation.description: Estimates a probability density, a regression function, or their derivatives using local polynomials. A fast binned implementation over an equally spaced grid is used.
translation.usage:
locpoly(x, y=None, drv=0, degree=None, kernel="normal",
        bandwidth, gridsize=401, bwdisc=25,
        range_x=None, binned=False, truncate=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric sample. Missing values are not accepted.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: Response values, the same length as x. None computes a density estimate.

arguments.name: drv
arguments.text: Order of derivative to be estimated.

arguments.name: degree
arguments.text: Degree of the local polynomial. Must be at least drv. None uses drv + 1.

arguments.name: kernel
arguments.text: Accepted and ignored, as in R. The fit uses a Gaussian kernel.

arguments.name: bandwidth
arguments.text: Kernel bandwidth. A single number, or a vector of length gridsize for a bandwidth that varies with location. Required, and every value must be positive.

arguments.name: gridsize
arguments.text: Number of equally spaced grid points.

arguments.name: bwdisc
arguments.text: Number of logarithmically spaced bandwidths on which bandwidth is discretised.

arguments.name: range_x
arguments.text: Minimum and maximum values of x at which to compute the estimate. This is range.x in R. None extends a density range by 5 percent and uses the data range for a regression.

arguments.name: binned
arguments.text: If true, and y is given, x and y are grid counts rather than raw data. range_x is then required.

arguments.name: truncate
arguments.text: If true, data outside range_x are ignored.

translation.details: Local polynomial fitting with a kernel weight estimates a density, a regression function, or their derivatives. Density estimation bins the data with the existing linbin crate. Regression estimation bins the pairs with rlbin. The fit is locpol, which solves the local systems with linpack. An equally spaced grid makes the computation fast.
translation.value: If y is given, a local polynomial regression estimate of E[Y|X] or its derivative. If y is omitted, a local polynomial estimate of the density of x or its derivative. The result is a dictionary with x, the grid, and y, the smoothed estimates.
translation.example:
from mass import geyser
from kernsmooth import locpoly
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = geyser["duration"]
est = locpoly(x, bandwidth=0.25)
plt.plot(est["x"], est["y"])

y = geyser["waiting"]
plt.figure()
plt.plot(x, y, linestyle="none", marker="o")
fit = locpoly(x, y, bandwidth=0.25)
plt.plot(fit["x"], fit["y"])
